one_liner: Senior Army contracting officer-level specialist at the Columbia, MD annex (cyber mission) who plans acquisitions, negotiates prices and terms, and administers complex contracts.
fit_summary: This GG-13 role requires a bachelor's degree, a year of hands-on contracting (acquisition strategy, market research and solicitations, cost and price analysis, complex negotiations) and the ability to obtain SCI eligibility. Daniel's proposal and purchasing work at IEM is contractor-side and below this level, so skip it.
eligibility: Basic requirement: a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution (transcripts required). The pre-2000 DoD/military exemptions won't apply to you.

One year of specialized experience covering all four areas: implementing acquisition strategies, pre-award work (market research, solicitations), cost and price analysis, and participating in complex negotiations and contract administration.
Must be able to obtain and keep a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance, which typically involves a TS/SCI investigation and possibly a polygraph.
Hiring path is listed as public, but the 'Who May Apply' text says applicants must select an employment authority category and provide proof.
This is a DoD Cyber Excepted Service position, so it is not in the competitive service, and the two-page resume limit does not apply.
strategy: Skip this one: it needs a year of hands-on contracting (acquisition strategy, cost and price analysis, complex negotiations) plus SCI eligibility, and his proposal and purchasing work at IEM was contractor-side and below this level.

Entry-level GS-1102 contract specialist roles open to the public at GS-7/9, or Virginia and Prince William County procurement jobs, are the realistic way to turn his proposal and procurement work into a contracting career.
His policy and emergency management strengths fit FEMA, Virginia VDEM, local emergency management or legislative offices, so prioritize those postings.
resume_bullets: Found multimillion-dollar opportunities in SAM.gov, GovWin and the DHS acquisition forecast, and led proposal writing (2019–2024).
Procured supplies and set up vendor relationships for COVID-19 sites in six states (2021–2022).
interview_questions: Walk us through an acquisition strategy you developed and why you chose that contract type.
How do you determine a price is fair and reasonable when limited competition exists?
Describe a complex negotiation you led or participated in and what you achieved.
How do you handle a contractor that is failing to meet performance terms post-award?
watch_outs: SCI clearance is required, which means a lengthy investigation and possibly a polygraph.
The posting requires a bachelor's degree, and transcripts must be submitted.
The specialized experience is highly technical contracting work that your known background likely does not cover. There is also no promotion potential beyond GG-13.
